name: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with multiple affected family members
Progressive chronic kidney disease with tubulointerstitial fibrosis on biopsy
Minimal or absent proteinuria despite progressive renal impairment
Identification of pathogenic variants in UMOD, MUC1, or REN genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history plus progressive renal failure with genetic confirmation or characteristic biopsy findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for definitive diagnosis; kidney biopsy may show nonspecific tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Familial autosomal dominant pattern of chronic kidney disease

searchTerms: little or no protein in urine
gout attacks from high uric acid

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: mild low red blood cell count

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or small kidneys without significant cysts
Occasional presence of small renal cysts
genetic: Pathogenic variants in UMOD gene (most common)
other: Kidney biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy and minimal glomerular involvement

distinguishingFeatures: More severe renal impairment at presentation
Presence of medullary cysts on imaging
Overlapping clinical features but distinct genetic mutations
May have more prominent cystic changes
Multiple large renal cysts on imaging
Dominant or recessive inheritance but with cystic phenotype
Often associated with liver cysts and hypertension

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure inconsistent with typical ADTKD course
Presence of heavy proteinuria or nephrotic syndrome
Early onset hypertension with severe systemic involvement
references: Olinger E, et al. Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: clinical and genetic features. Kidney Int. 2019.
Bleyer AJ, et al. Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: diagnosis and management. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2017.
commonPitfalls: Often misdiagnosed as chronic glomerulonephritis due to bland urinary sediment and progressive renal insufficiency.
Family history may be overlooked, leading to missed autosomal dominant inheritance pattern.
Renal cysts, if present, may lead to confusion with polycystic kidney disease.
Proteinuria is typically mild or absent, so nephrotic-range proteinuria should prompt reconsideration of diagnosis.

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Absence or paucity of renal cysts on imaging in early disease; ADTKD typically has few or no cysts, especially in childhood.
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern and later age of onset compared to autosomal recessive forms.
ADTKD is now considered to encompass medullary cystic kidney disease; genetic testing (e.g., UMOD, MUC1 mutations) distinguishes subtypes.

ruleOutCriteria: Nephrotic-range proteinuria (>3.5 g/day) is not consistent with ADTKD.
Absence of family history of chronic kidney disease across multiple generations makes ADTKD unlikely.
Presence of significant hematuria or active urinary sediment excludes ADTKD.
